Synopsis:
    TerraPower (Bill Gates-backed) targets 2034 for first UK Natrium reactor deployment, marking its first international market. Each sodium-cooled unit delivers 345 MW baseload with storage capability up to 500 MW. Cost target is sub-£100/MWh, competitive with solar-and-battery. HALEU fuel supply is being secured domestically in UK and US, reducing Russian dependency. A UK subsidiary is being established near Liverpool. Corporate offtake partnerships (similar to the US Meta deal) are being explored for the UK.

Q01. Is the content's main message about EU energy, EU commodities, German power market prices, German energy economics?
Relevance: NO — The article focuses exclusively on UK and US nuclear developments. No reference to EU energy markets, German power prices, or broader continental European energy economics.

Q02. Is the content confirming already known information or reporting very new/uncertain risks?
Risk score: 25 — SMR development in the UK is a known policy direction. TerraPower's UK ambitions add some specificity (2034 timeline, sub-£100/MWh cost target), but the story broadly confirms an already anticipated trajectory rather than introducing genuinely unexpected risk.
